title: What is NuGet?
description: An introduction to NuGet, the package manager for .NET.

data.text: NuGet is the package manager for .NET. Instead of copying third-party source code into your repository, you reference a **package**: a versioned, self-contained unit of compiled assemblies, content files, and metadata. NuGet resolves the dependency graph, downloads the exact versions you need, and keeps them out of source control.

Packages come from **feeds**. `nuget.org` is the public feed maintained by Microsoft; teams also run private feeds (Azure Artifacts, GitHub Packages, Artifactory, or a local folder) for internal libraries. NuGet is installed with the .NET SDK, so if `dotnet --version` works, NuGet is available.

terms.definition: A zip archive containing the compiled assemblies, optional content files, and a .nuspec manifest with id, version, and dependencies.
The entry in your .csproj that declares a package and its version, for example <PackageReference Include="Newtonsoft.Json" Version="13.0.3" />.
The step that reads PackageReference entries, downloads packages from feeds, and writes the resolved graph to obj/project.assets.json.
A machine-wide cache (~/.nuget/packages on Windows) so the same version is downloaded only once and shared by all projects.

data.title: Add a package and restore it
data.content: `dotnet add package` updates the project file; a build or explicit restore then downloads the package.
data.code:
dotnet new console -n NugetDemo
cd NugetDemo
dotnet add package Newtonsoft.Json --version 13.0.3
dotnet restore
dotnet run

data.title: The resulting project file
data.content: NuGet writes a PackageReference into the .csproj. This file is the source of truth and should be committed.

data.title: Interview framing
data.text: Be ready to explain the difference between **direct** and **transitive** dependencies: you declare direct references, and NuGet pulls transitive dependencies automatically. The resolved set is what actually ships, so a CVE can come from a package you never named.

data.title: Common mistakes
items: Committing the `bin/` or `obj/` folders (restore output) instead of just the project file and packages config.
Assuming `dotnet restore` is always needed — `dotnet build`, `dotnet run`, and `dotnet test` restore automatically.
Editing versions in `project.assets.json` — that file is generated and overwritten on every restore.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: NuGet manages .NET dependencies through versioned .nupkg packages
PackageReference in the .csproj is the source of truth
Restore resolves the full graph and caches packages machine-wide
Packages come from public or private feeds
data.takeaway: NuGet turns dependency management into a declarative, reproducible process instead of manually copying binaries.
